subject: english
title: Intermediate Examination 2026 English (Set A) - Section A

questions.question: Ankita ________ come yet; the whole class is waiting for her. (Choose the correct option)
questions.explanation: 'Yet' with a singular subject ('Ankita') and present waiting context takes present perfect negative 'hasn't'.

questions.question: Let us organise a get-together party. (Choose the correct passive voice)
options: We should be organising a get-together party.
Get-together party must be surely organised.
A get-together party should be organised.
A get-together party would be organised by us.
questions.explanation: Proposals starting with 'Let us + V1' commonly convert to passive using 'should be + V3' ('A get-together party should be organised.').

questions.question: Milan is ________ Italian city. (Choose the correct option)
questions.explanation: 'Italian' starts with a vowel sound (/ɪ/), so indefinite article 'an' is used.

questions.question: Rolls-Royce cars are ________. (Choose the correct option)
questions.explanation: Rolls-Royce is well known for luxury, expensive cars.

questions.question: ________ languages does Aryan speak? (Choose the correct option)
questions.explanation: 'How many' is used before plural countable nouns ('languages').

questions.question: That's my book. Can I have ________ back please? (Choose the correct option)
questions.explanation: Singular object pronoun 'it' refers back to 'my book'.

questions.question: Sunaina loves ________ to music. (Choose the correct option)
questions.explanation: 'Loves to listen to music' is grammatically complete with the preposition 'to' before 'music'.

questions.question: There ________ an armchair in my bedroom. (Choose the correct option)
questions.explanation: Singular noun phrase 'an armchair' takes singular verb 'is'.

questions.question: The boys ________ very tired today because they were at a party last night. (Choose the correct option)
questions.explanation: 'Today' with plural subject 'The boys' requires present plural 'are'.

questions.question: Rohini said, "I have a stomach-ache." (Choose the correct option)
options: Rohini says that she have a stomach-ache.
Rohini said that she had got a stomach-ache.
Rohini said that she has a stomach-ache.
Rohini said that she got a stomach-ache.
questions.explanation: In past narration, 'have' shifts back to past/past perfect ('had got' in the given choices).

questions.question: The meeting ________ at half-past eight. (Choose the correct option)
questions.explanation: Singular subject 'The meeting' takes 'starts' for scheduled/timetabled events.

questions.question: Choose the correct meaning of 'Docile':
questions.explanation: 'Docile' means ready to accept control or instruction; obedient.

questions.question: It is impossible to do this. (Choose the correct passive voice)
options: This is impossible to be done.
To do this by it is impossible.
It is impossible to have done this.
questions.explanation: Infinitive passive 'to be done' expresses passive capability/feasibility after 'impossible'.

questions.question: "Call the witness," said the judge. (Choose the correct indirect speech)
options: The judge commanded to call the witness.
The judge commanded them to call the witness.
The judge commanded that the witness be called.
The judge commanded the witness to be called.
questions.explanation: Mandative subjunctive 'commanded that the witness be called' is a standard formal indirect form for an official command.

questions.question: The doctor advised him to rest for ________ days. (Choose the correct option)
questions.explanation: 'A few' means a small number of plural countable days.

questions.question: A thorough search of the aircraft was carried ________ in the airport. (Choose the correct option)
questions.explanation: 'Carry out' means conduct or execute a search/inspection.

questions.question: As she became tired, error began to creep ________ her work. (Choose the correct option)
questions.explanation: 'Creep into' means to gradually enter or appear unnoticed.

questions.question: Choose a one-word substitution for 'The absence of government in a country':
questions.explanation: 'Anarchy' is a state of disorder due to absence of government or authority.

questions.question: Choose a one-word substitution for 'Ceremony of crowning a king':
questions.explanation: 'Coronation' is the ceremony of crowning a sovereign.

questions.question: Choose the correct meaning of "Blow one's own trumpet":
questions.explanation: 'Blow one's own trumpet' means to boast about or praise oneself.

questions.question: The two friends had a ________ talk after a long time. (Choose the correct option)
questions.explanation: 'Heart-to-heart talk' means a sincere, candid, and intimate conversation.

questions.question: Choose the correct antonym of 'Humility':
questions.explanation: 'Pride' (arrogance/self-importance) is the opposite of 'humility' (modesty).

questions.question: Choose the correct synonym of 'Relish':
questions.explanation: 'Relish' means to enjoy greatly.

questions.question: Choose the correct antonym of 'Scorn':
questions.explanation: 'Admiration' is the opposite of 'scorn' (disdain/contempt).

questions.question: Choose the correct synonym of 'Jealous':
questions.explanation: 'Envious' is a direct synonym of 'jealous'.

questions.question: The ________ duty of every citizen is to respect the country. (Choose the correct option)
questions.explanation: 'First and foremost' means primary or most important.

questions.question: Make sure you ________ at least two hours before your flight. (Choose the correct option)
questions.explanation: 'Check in' is the standard aviation/hotel term for registering arrival.

questions.question: Sheetal ran fast. She wanted to win the race. (Choose the correct combination)
options: Sheetal running fast for winning the race.
Sheetal is running fast to win the race.
Running fast is Sheetal for winning the race.
Sheetal ran fast to win the race.
questions.explanation: 'Sheetal ran fast to win the race.' preserves past tense ('ran') and expresses purpose with 'to win'.

questions.question: He broke the lock ________ a hammer. (Choose the correct option)
questions.explanation: 'With the help of' indicates using a tool/instrument ('a hammer').

questions.question: Abriti has decided ________ more. (Choose the correct option)
questions.explanation: 'Decided + to + base verb (earn)' is the standard infinitive structure.

questions.question: You need to buy ________ refrigerator. (Choose the correct option)
questions.explanation: 'Refrigerator' begins with a consonant sound (/r/), so 'a' is used.

questions.question: We saw a ________ of lions at the sanctuary. (Choose the correct option)
questions.explanation: The collective noun for a group of lions is a 'pride'.

questions.question: Choose the odd one out:
questions.explanation: 'Mustard' is an oilseed crop, whereas wheat, paddy, and barley are cereal grains.

questions.question: I like the books ________ have interesting stories. (Choose the correct option)
questions.explanation: Relative pronoun 'that' refers to non-human objects ('the books') as the subject of 'have'.

questions.question: I have no ________ to you going for a movie. (Choose the correct option)
questions.explanation: Noun 'objection' fits naturally after 'no' before 'to'.

questions.question: You ________ cross the road when the traffic light is red. (Choose the correct option)
questions.explanation: 'Musn't' (mustn't) expresses prohibition against crossing on a red signal.

questions.question: ________ have that dress specially made? (Choose the correct option)
questions.explanation: 'Did you have that dress specially made?' forms a grammatical past question.

questions.question: Learning ________ is not easy. (Choose the correct option)
questions.explanation: Names of languages like 'Sanskrit' take no article in general reference.

questions.question: I saw two crows ________ poking their heads at the flowerpot. (Choose the correct option)
questions.explanation: Present participle 'playing' describes the ongoing action observed.

questions.question: Please have ________ more rice, you haven't taken much. (Choose the correct option)
questions.explanation: 'Some' is used in positive offers/requests for uncountable 'rice'.

questions.question: Work ________ to score good marks. (Choose the correct option)
questions.explanation: 'Work hard' means put in diligent effort ('hardly' means scarcely/almost not).

questions.question: Someone was knocking ________ the door. (Choose the correct option)
questions.explanation: 'Knock at the door' is the standard preposition usage.

questions.question: She needs some new clothes, ________? (Choose the correct option)
questions.explanation: Positive simple present statement with singular 'She' takes negative tag 'doesn't she'.

questions.question: The synonym of 'Marvellous' is ________. (Choose the correct option)
questions.explanation: 'Wonderful' is a synonym of 'marvellous'.

questions.question: The antonym of 'Fixed' is ________. (Choose the correct option)
questions.explanation: 'Undecided' contrasts with 'fixed' (settled/decided).

questions.question: The synonym of 'Hoard' is ________. (Choose the correct option)
questions.explanation: 'Hoard' means to accumulate and store away.

questions.question: The antonym of 'Moisture' is ________. (Choose the correct option)
questions.explanation: 'Dryness' is the opposite of 'moisture'.

questions.question: Sumit asked her if she was ill. (Choose the correct direct narration)
options: Sumit said to her, "Are you ill?"
Sumit said to her, "Is she ill?"
questions.explanation: 'Asked her if she was ill' converts back to direct yes/no question 'Sumit said to her, "Are you ill?"'

questions.question: He requested me to keep the door open. (Choose the correct direct narration)
options: He said to me, "Please keep the door open."
He will say, "Keep the door open."
He said, "Never keep the door open."
questions.explanation: 'Requested me to keep...' corresponds to 'He said to me, "Please keep the door open."'.

questions.question: Choose the correctly spelt word:
questions.explanation: 'Jaundice' is the correct spelling.

questions.question: India will win the world cup. That is certain. (Choose the correct combination)
options: It is certain that India will win the world cup.
India will certainly win the world cup.
Certainly, India will win the world cup.
India will win the world cup certainly.
questions.explanation: 'It is certain that India will win the world cup.' combines the two sentences cleanly into a complex sentence.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence:
options: The boys runs fast in the race.
The boys run fast in the race.
The boy run fast in the race.
The boy running fast in the race.
questions.explanation: Plural subject 'The boys' takes base plural verb 'run'.

questions.question: I got late for the flight ________ there was so much traffic on the road. (Choose the correct option)
questions.explanation: 'Because' gives the reason for getting late.

questions.question: We located the key ________ the lock. (Choose the correct option)
questions.explanation: 'The key for the lock' is the natural prepositional phrase.

questions.question: Choose the correct meaning of "To keep one's temper":
questions.explanation: 'To keep one's temper' means to stay calm and composed.

questions.question: Choose the correct meaning of "To cry wolf":
questions.explanation: 'To cry wolf' means to raise a false alarm.

questions.question: They decided to ________ his number in the yellow pages. (Choose the correct option)
questions.explanation: 'Look up' means to search for information in a directory, book, or list.

questions.question: After a prolonged suffering he 'passed away'. (Choose the correct option of the underlined phrase)
questions.explanation: 'Passed away' is a polite euphemism for died/expired.

questions.question: We have no alternative plan to ________ on. (Choose the correct option)
questions.explanation: 'Fall back on' means to turn to as a backup plan or resource.

questions.question: She came across some papers she was looking for. (Choose the correct option of the underlined words)
questions.explanation: 'Came across' means found or met by chance.

questions.question: What figure of speech has been used in "My Grandmother's House"?
questions.explanation: Kamala Das uses similes such as 'my blood turned cold like the moon' in 'My Grandmother's House'.

questions.question: ________ is the prime instrument of nation building.
questions.explanation: In 'Bharat is My Home', Dr. Zakir Hussain emphasizes education as the prime instrument of nation building.

questions.question: "I Have a Dream" is part of a ________.
questions.explanation: 'I Have a Dream' is Martin Luther King, Jr.'s famous 1963 speech delivered at the Lincoln Memorial.

questions.question: "We saw embers losing their cruel redness" is taken from:
questions.explanation: This line appears in Keki N. Daruwala's poem 'Fire-Hymn'.

questions.question: Indian peasants are poorer than their ________ counterparts.
questions.explanation: In 'India Through a Traveller's Eyes', Pearl S. Buck compares Indian peasants with their Chinese counterparts.

questions.question: John Donne feels that ________ is very hopeless.
questions.explanation: In 'Sweetest Love, I Do Not Goe', John Donne remarks on how feeble and impatient man's power/hope can be.

questions.question: ________ says that he is having a heart failure.
questions.explanation: In Anton Chekhov's 'A Marriage Proposal', hypochondriac Lomov repeatedly complains of heart palpitations/failure.

questions.question: In traditional birth infant and mother mortality is ________.
questions.explanation: In 'A Child is Born', Germaine Greer notes greater infant and maternal mortality in traditional/unassisted birth settings.

questions.question: "But believe that I shall make speedier journeys" is taken from:
options: Sweetest Love I Do Not Goe
questions.explanation: This line is from John Donne's 'Sweetest Love, I Do Not Goe'.

questions.question: Lomov is a man conscious of ________.
questions.explanation: In 'A Marriage Proposal', Lomov is deeply concerned about property and social class standing.

questions.question: The ________ has become dumb to see the leafless trees.
questions.explanation: In 'Now the Leaves are Falling Fast', the nightingale becomes dumb and will not come to help.

questions.question: The press enjoys the ________ of the public.
questions.explanation: In 'How Free is the Press', Dorothy L. Sayers discusses how the press exploits public helplessness/apathy.

questions.question: For all the ills in India, the writer blames ________.
questions.explanation: In 'India Through a Traveller's Eyes', Pearl S. Buck attributes much of India's poverty and ills to British rule.

questions.question: Benjy owned a ________.
questions.explanation: In H. E. Bates's 'The Earth', Benjy buys a Ford van.

questions.question: Seibei's parents knew that Seibei often went out to buy ________.
questions.explanation: In 'The Artist', Seibei's parents knew he went out to look for and buy gourds.

questions.question: Advertisers contribute to the ________ of the newspaper.
questions.explanation: In 'How Free is the Press', advertising revenue is a major financial pillar of newspapers.

questions.question: The poet is ________ the snake.
questions.explanation: In D. H. Lawrence's 'Snake', the poet feels a sense of honour and awe toward the royal snake.

questions.question: "Tower of silence" is related to ________ religion.
questions.explanation: A Tower of Silence (Dakhma) is associated with Zoroastrian/Parsi funeral practice.

questions.question: ________ is sweltering with the heat of injustice and oppression.
questions.explanation: In 'I Have a Dream', Martin Luther King, Jr. refers to Mississippi as sweltering with injustice and oppression.

questions.question: Every human death by starvation is preceded by a long period of ________.
questions.explanation: In 'India Through a Traveller's Eyes', Pearl S. Buck writes that death by starvation follows a long period of anxiety.

questions.question: Nanukaka has a unique quality of telling ________.
questions.explanation: In 'A Pinch of Snuff', Nanukaka is adept at spinning clever, plausible lies/fabrications to get things done.

questions.question: ________ discrimination was disapproved by Martin Luther King, Jr.
questions.explanation: Martin Luther King, Jr. campaigned against racial discrimination.

questions.question: Natalia and ________ are quarrelling for the Ox-Meadows.
questions.explanation: In 'A Marriage Proposal', Natalia and Lomov argue over ownership of Ox Meadows.

questions.question: English is a ________.
questions.explanation: English is commonly described as a 'window to the world'.

questions.question: The Norman Conquest made England into little more than a colony of ________.
questions.explanation: The Norman Conquest of 1066 brought strong French/Norman influence over England.

questions.question: Langland is a well known writer of ________ English literature.
questions.explanation: William Langland is a major poet of the Middle English period.

questions.question: The Anglo-Saxons invaded England in the ________ century.
questions.explanation: Anglo-Saxon settlement/invasion of Britain is dated to the fifth century AD.

questions.question: In the poem 'Snake', Lawrence denounces the artificialities of ________ life.
questions.explanation: D. H. Lawrence contrasts natural instinct with the artificialities of modern life.

questions.question: Indian English came into existence in ________ century.
questions.explanation: In the Bihar Board curriculum, Indian English literature/usage is traced to the 19th century.

questions.question: Seibei took to ________ after giving up collecting gourds.
questions.explanation: In 'The Artist', after his gourd was confiscated, Seibei turned passionately to painting pictures.

questions.question: "Nothing can equal the seeds sown by our ancestors" is from:
questions.explanation: This sentiment reflects Mahatma Gandhi's view of ancestral heritage in 'Indian Civilization and Culture'.

questions.question: ________ is known as the Nightingale of India.
questions.explanation: Sarojini Naidu is famously known as the Nightingale of India.

questions.question: "His footprints are not found in any file of ________ yard."
questions.explanation: In 'Macavity: The Mystery Cat', Macavity's footprints are not found in any file of Scotland Yard.

questions.question: Different varieties of English will together form a ________.
questions.explanation: In the Bihar Board History of English textbook, global varieties of English relate to Standard Spoken English.

questions.question: ________ does not have the largest number of native speakers.
questions.explanation: Chinese (Mandarin) has the largest number of native speakers, not English.

questions.question: Who were the rulers of ancient Egypt?
questions.explanation: Pharaohs (spelt 'Pharoahs' in the option) were the rulers of ancient Egypt.

questions.question: ________ was more important than any other invention.
questions.explanation: In 'Ideas That Have Helped Mankind', Bertrand Russell highlights the invention of agriculture as crucial to human settlement and progress.

questions.question: ________ was Nanukaka's favourite dress.
questions.explanation: In 'A Pinch of Snuff', Nanukaka favoured a Jodhpuri coat and turban.

questions.question: ________ was influenced by Mahatma Gandhi.
questions.explanation: Martin Luther King, Jr. was deeply influenced by Mahatma Gandhi's philosophy of non-violence.

questions.question: Every newspaper lives in a precarious ________.
questions.explanation: In 'How Free is the Press', newspapers operate in a precarious financial/editorial balance.
